newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FDP hopeful of tax cut deal with SPD.
newsitem.headline: German FDP hopeful of tax cut deal with SPD.

text.p: Germany's Free Democrats (FDP), the junior partner in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, on Monday said it was optimistic of reaching a compromise with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on tax reforms.
But FDP leader Wolfgang Gerhardt told reporters Germany's economic plight meant that a deal must be reached before Easter and coalition tax cut plans must not be watered down.
"Before we go into the Easter break it must be clear how the tax reform will look," Gerhardt said after a meeting of FDP leaders.

Kohl will head a coalition team at tax talks with the SPD which begins at 1400 GMT -- a crucial meeting which could almost at a stroke sidestep the parliamentary barrier to passing tax reforms to fight record post-war unemployment.
The FDP is not prepared to compromise on new income tax rates which would start at 15 percent and rise to 39 percent, Gerhardt said. Current tax brackets run from 26 to 53 percent.

He said the FDP was prepared to negotiate on some aspects of abolishing tax breaks to finance the tax cuts, but the overall lightening of the tax burden could not be reduced from the coalition's goal of 30 billion marks ($17.9 billion).

Gerhardt said that a moderate increase in value-added tax -- something opposed by the SPD -- should be considered to help finance the reform. But that element should only come into the tax calculations when new direct tax rates are confirmed.

Quick action on the tax reform, as well as agreement on passing savings measures currently blocked by the SPD through its parliamentary upper house majority could yield quick benefits for Germany's economy, he said.
"We have a justified hope that we can bring about a change in trend on the jobs market by mid-year," Gerhardt said.
